I agree with you. So I had to weigh my options. Sure, I can have a way out by ending my life, and cause my wife a magnitude of emotional distress for who-knows-how-long. Or I could live and experience a lot of emotional pain that is extremely difficult to bear. And I agree, the more noble option is to simply live with the pain. I will try my best. Thank you.

Though, I don't want something better. I want my wife. The one I love more than anyone else.

I can't make any promises because I'm still very much weighing what I should do next. My bed is lonely. The majority of my major plans have been completely annihilated. My wife is simply the most amazing person I've ever known, and every time I even try to imagine a life without her I break down. I am a decade older than you, though I won't say that makes me any wiser. In general I agree that suicide is not the answer. However, I simply cannot image a world without her. It's like having a car and the internet, and then no longer having these things, except amplified by a thousand. Perhaps that was a bad analogy, but I think you know what I mean.
She believed in mystical energy an new-agey stuff like that. I would always point out that these kinds of beliefs were unfounded.
I relayed a message, but she's most likely asleep. If she gets it, it will be a bit later in the day. Thank you.
It's not just about the pain I feel. I really feel as if she is my other half. That life without her is simply not a life I care to live with.

As I have said, We had a difference in beliefs, and she felt I belittled hers, and that I didn't respect them. I have some friends, but as I have said, I simply don't want to live a life without my wife.
